key_insight: Solaris is the first action-conditioned video world model that simulates consistent multi-view, multi-agent observations by combining a multiplayer data collection system with a multi-view generative model.
problem_solved: Existing video world models are limited to single-agent, single-view settings and cannot capture the interactions and coherent observations that arise in multiplayer environments.
method: Develop a multiplayer data system for robust, continuous, automated collection of synchronized multi-player, multi-view video data in Minecraft.
Train an action-conditioned generative world model that predicts future video observations for multiple agents and views simultaneously.
Enforce multi-view consistency via shared world-state representations and cross-view supervision so simulated views remain coherent across agents and time.
impact: Enables realistic multi-agent video simulation for planning, multi-agent RL, and virtual-world research, reducing reliance on single-view assumptions and improving realism for downstream tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing Minecraft servers/clients feeding synchronized multi-player multi-view video into the Solaris data system

paper_title: Solaris: Building a Multiplayer Video World Model in Minecraft
paper_authors: Georgy Savva, Oscar Michel, Daohan Lu, Suppakit Waiwitlikhit, Timothy Meehan
